route: O-1 (extraordinary ability in the arts, or extraordinary achievement in motion pictures or television)

permit.applies: A United States employer, a United States agent, or a foreign employer through a United States agent petitions USCIS on Form I-129; the performer then seeks the visa or admission.
permit.first: The approved petition, which needs a written advisory opinion from the consulting peer group, labor and/or management organization.

fees.what: Form I-129, petition for O nonimmigrant worker, 1 to 25 named beneficiaries (small employers and nonprofits pay half)
Asylum Program Fee, any I-129 petitioner (small employer USD 300; nonprofit none)
Premium processing, O-1 or O-2 petition (optional)

permit.union: Consultation is mandatory before an O-1 petition is approved: for motion picture or television work, with the appropriate union representing the performer's occupational peers and a management organization; for other arts, with a peer group, which may include a labor organization. The opinions are advisory.
permit.eligibility: Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction. Distinction means a high level of achievement in the field of arts evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that a person described as prominent is renowned, leading, or well-known in the field of arts.

sources.title: 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38), definition of United States (GovInfo, 2023 edition)
sources.said: The term "United States", except as otherwise specifically herein provided, when used in a geographical sense, means the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands of the United States, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(o) Aliens of extraordinary ability or achievement
sources.said: An O-1 or O-2 petition may only be filed by a United States employer, a United States agent, or a foreign employer through a United States agent. … is mandatory before a petition for an O-1 or O-2 classification can be approved. … who will be working on a motion picture or television production, consultation shall be made with the appropriate union representing the alien's occupational peers and a management organization in the area of the alien's ability. … Consultation with a peer group in the area of the alien's ability (which may include a labor organization), or a person or persons with expertise in the area of the alien's ability, is required in an O-1 petition for an alien of extraordinary ability. … Consultations are advisory and are not binding on the Service. … Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction. Distinction means a high level of achievement in the field of arts evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that a person described as prominent is renowned, leading, or well-known in the field of arts. … shall be valid for a period of time determined by the Director to be necessary to accomplish the event or activity, not to exceed 3 years. … An extension of stay may be authorized in increments of up to 1 year for an O-1 or O-2 beneficiary to continue or complete the same event or activity

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 106.2 USCIS fees
sources.said: Petition for O Nonimmigrant Worker with 1 to 25 named beneficiaries: $1,055. … Cross Reference Link to an amendment published at 91 FR 61984 , Sept. 30, 2026. … Filed by a small employer as defined in § 106.1(f) : $300.

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 106.4 Premium processing service
sources.said: Petition for classification of a nonimmigrant described in section 101(a)(15)(O)(i) or (ii) of the INA—$2,965. … Petition for classification of a nonimmigrant described in section 101(a)(15)(O)(i) or (ii) of the Act: 15 business days.

note: The US Virgin Islands are part of the United States under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38)), so a performer works there on the United States' O-1. The petition is valid for the time needed for the event or activity, at most three years, and the stay can be extended in increments of up to a year to continue or complete it. The fee section carries a cross-reference to an amendment published at 91 FR 61984 (30 September 2026), not read (federalregister.gov and ecfr.gov now bot-check this client), so the fees may since have changed. The consular visa fee isn't included: travel.state.gov blocks this client.
